excitation_report: Typed ODE excitation compares the full child vs parent 2-state systems on the target n-trajectory. sigma=0.05 (abs std on dn_dt, ~0.4% of the ~12 peak flux). NEW term (aperture_feedback_gain*(g-g_eq)/(1+|g-g_eq|/aperture_feedback_scale) in the g-equation): peak effect 2.10 in n-units = ~42x sigma, strongest near t=150 (accumulated steady g-offset). All standard n-equation terms are strongly excited over the run: hop flux |0.02*(N-2n)| up to ~12, crowding ~2.3, aperture coupling ~2.5 at n~650 with g~O(1) — each thousands of sigma. First (runaway) parameter set with aperture_time=8 gave 3527x sigma via g->inf; shortened aperture_time to 2 so relaxation cap (1/aperture_time=0.5) exceeds the drive (aperture_response+gain*scale=0.26), keeping g bounded (~1) and n within [0,N_total] while the new term stays clearly visible.

Roles confirmed against structure: n is the target state, g is a genuine second dynamic state with its own equation (kept, not frozen), t is the only axis, remaining 12 symbols are fixed parameters. Parameters chosen for physical, bounded relaxation: symmetric hop rates (linear balance at N_total/2=500), N_total=1000>n0=800, modest crowding and aperture coupling so g and n stay bounded. The evolution's new mechanism is the saturating positive-feedback term in the g-equation; aperture_time=2 was chosen so relaxation caps above the total g-drive, preventing the g-runaway seen at aperture_time=8 while the new term still marks the n-trajectory at ~42x sigma. Feedback gain/scale kept inside the suggested hint ranges.

scenario_text: A container is divided into two compartments connected by a small opening, holding a fixed total number of gas particles that hop between sides. Starting from an uneven split, the particle count in one compartment relaxes toward an even balance driven by the greater number of accessible microstates near equality. Observers track the population of one compartment as it evolves toward balance.
